methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a Norfolk native represent grassroots knowledge distribution outside traditional tech hubs, signaling potential for peer-to-peer skill building that could deepen capabilities in military-adjacent regions.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Data center concentration in NoVA explicitly widens the urban-rural divide, reinforcing concentrated infrastructure and capital investment while rural areas lack access to the economic benefits or capability development.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce suggests platform-driven automation creating broad but shallow adoption, where workers must adapt to AI tools without necessarily developing deep technical capabilities.

signals.title: Virginia journalist: Fired by AI - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: A Virginia journalist being replaced by AI without visible reskilling pathways or distributed capability development signals neither depth nor distribution materializing, particularly outside metro centers.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., Meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI Help Assistant - DVIDS
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard deploying a sophisticated AI assistant demonstrates deep capability development, but within a concentrated federal/defense institution rather than distributed civilian workforce, reinforcing hub-based expertise.
